description.en: Rav Chisda studied under Rav and Rav Huna in Sura. He eventually got into a quarrel with the latter, causing him to leave and set up his own academy in the town of Kafri. After many years, they both regretted this and reconciled.
description.he: רב חסדא למד עם רב ועם רב הונא בסורא. לאחר שהסתכסך עם רב הונא, עזב וייסד ישיבה עצמאית בעירו כפרי. כעבור שנים הביעו שניהם חרטה והתפייסו.

en.title: Rav Chisda's Greatness
en.prompt: Rav Chisda, despite being a student of Rav Huna, may have been equal or even greater in wisdom than his teacher. Rabbi Ben-Zion Meir Hai Uziel, in his responsa collection 'Mishpetei Uziel,' discusses the Talmudic debate on the relative greatness of these two sages.

en.title: The Analytical Brilliance of Rav Chisda
en.ai_title: The Analytical Brilliance of Rav Chisda
en.prompt: Rav Chisda's sharp analytical skills and deep respect for his master, Rav, exemplify the intellectual rigor and mutual respect that are hallmarks of Talmudic study. The eighteenth-century chronicle Seder HaDorot by Rabbi Yechiel Heilprin offers a detailed account of the lives and scholarly achievements of Tanaim and Amoraim, the rabbis of the Mishnah and Talmud.

en.title: Rav Chisda vs. Rav Huna
en.prompt: The frequent and direct legal disagreements between Rav Chisda and Rav Huna offer a fascinating glimpse into the dynamic nature of Jewish law and its interpretation. This text from the Babylonian Talmud captures the spirited debates between these two prominent Amoraim on various legal issues, such as the purity required for reciting the Shema and the validity of a divorce delivered by an agent.
